newsitem.title: CHINA: Sakakibara to be appointed vice MOF minister-paper.
newsitem.headline: Sakakibara to be appointed vice MOF minister-paper.

text.p: Influential Japanese finance official Eisuke Sakakibara, currently director of the Ministry of Finance's (MOF) International Finance Bureau, is poised to take over as Vice Finance Minister for International Affairs, a Japanese daily reported on Friday.
The Sankei Shimbun said that Sakakibara will be officially appointed vice minister in mid-July, taking over from Takatoshi Kato, who will retire from the post.

Sakakibara's promotion would put him in formal charge of MOF negotitations with other Group of Seven (G7) nations and would be seen as a recognition of his success in turning around the yen's precipitous rise to above 80 yen to the dollar in 1995.

"I don't know anything (about the new appointment)," Sakakibara said on Friday, when asked about the Sankei report. He is in Shanghai accompanying Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka's visit to China. Both will return to Tokyo later today.
